record.original_question: A Siegel disk is guaranteed by the presence of a suitable periodic point, namely a Siegel point. Is there an analogous kind of point or other intrinsic dynamical marker whose existence would guarantee that the map has a Herman ring?

evidence.quote: Siegel discs and Herman rings show quasi-periodic dynamics, but the latter are seen in annular domains. This adds topological complexity and richness to dynamical classifications. Furthermore, a specific kind of periodic point known as a Siegel point guarantees the existence of a Siegel disk. Is there a point whose existence will guarantee the Herman ring’s existence?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a rational map of degree at least two (or, more generally, a transcendental meromorphic function on $\mathbb{C}$). Recall the Fatou–Julia decomposition: the Fatou set $F(f)$ is the set of points possessing a neighborhood on which the iterates $\{f^n\}$ form a normal family, and the Julia set is $J(f)=\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus F(f)$. A periodic Fatou component $U$ of period $p\ge 1$ is called

- a Siegel disk if $U$ is simply connected and $f^p|_U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ of the unit disk;
- a Herman ring if $U$ is conformally an annulus and $f^p|_U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation $w\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}w$ of a round annulus $\{1<|w|<r\}$.

A Siegel point of $f$ is a fixed (or periodic) point $z_0$ such that $f'(z_0)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ with $\alpha$ a Brjuno (or otherwise suitably Diophantine) irrational; the existence of such a periodic point guarantees the existence of a Siegel disk attached to $z_0$.

Question. Determine whether there exists an intrinsic dynamical marker for Herman rings analogous to a Siegel point for Siegel disks: that is, exhibit (or prove the nonexistence of) a property $\mathcal{P}$ — formulated as the existence of a distinguished point, periodic cycle, or other purely intrinsic dynamical/local invariant of $f$ — whose presence forces $f$ to possess a Herman ring, and conversely is detectable directly from $f$ without first constructing the Herman ring.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on Herman rings (December 2025). No published result provides an intrinsic local marker (analogous to a Siegel periodic point) that forces existence of a Herman ring; known existence proofs proceed via quasiconformal surgery from circle diffeomorphisms rather than from a local invariant of the map. No solution was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Herman Rings: Structure, Dynamics, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey collecting open problems on Herman rings of rational and transcendental meromorphic functions.
status_evidence.claim: The question of an intrinsic marker guaranteeing a Herman ring is listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic Dynamics and Herman Rings
status_evidence.snippet: Existence theorems for Herman rings are established via quasiconformal surgery from circle diffeomorphisms, not via a local periodic-point marker.
status_evidence.claim: No intrinsic local marker analogous to a Siegel point is known for Herman rings.

status_evidence.title: Complex dynamics - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Herman rings are constructed by Herman using Arnold's results on circle diffeomorphisms; no local linearization-type criterion is given.
status_evidence.claim: Standard sources do not provide an intrinsic marker forcing a Herman ring.
